user:
Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

Below are 24 candidate research ideas for this problem. Group them into 4-7 method families such that ideas in the same family share their core mechanism (not merely their goal). Give each family a short name.

[B1-g0-C1] Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive MVFA scoring
Replace test-set min-max with each branch's (and level's) leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores; keep the 0.5 fusion and max pooling.

[B1-g0-C2] Source-episode scale with support re-centring for inductive MVFA scoring
Learn each branch's scale on simulated few-shot episodes from the source modalities and set only its location from the K target supports, replacing test-set min-max.

[B1-g0-C3] Prototype-radius normalisation of MVFA's few-shot branch
Cluster support patch features into normal prototypes per level, score test patches by distance to the nearest prototype divided by its radius, and fuse with the support-normalised zero-shot branch using MVFA's unchanged rule.

[B1-g0-C4] Two-anchor scaling with support normals and synthetic lesions
Normalise each MVFA branch between the median score of support-normal patches and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into those supports, removing all test-set statistics.

[B1-g0-C5] Position-wise support normalisation of MVFA's branches
Normalise each branch's patch score by the leave-one-out support scores at the same grid position, shrunk towards the global support statistic, so anatomy-driven offsets are removed without test-set statistics.

[B1-g0-C6] Anchor-geometry normalisation of MVFA's zero-shot branch
Replace the softmax output of the zero-shot branch by the patch projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, and fuse them with MVFA's unchanged rule.

[B1-g1-o1] Position-wise low anchor and synthetic high anchor for inductive MVFA scoring
Normalise each branch per grid position between a shrunk position-wise median of leave-one-out support scores (low anchor) and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into the supports (high anchor), keeping MVFA's 0.5 fusion and max pooling.

[B1-g1-o2] Position-wise leave-one-out empirical CDF with neighbourhood pooling
Map each patch score through the empirical CDF of leave-one-out support scores from the same grid neighbourhood, mixed with the global support CDF according to how many reference values the neighbourhood holds.

[B1-g1-o3] Empirical CDF of anatomy residuals for inductive MVFA scoring
Subtract a shrunk position-wise median of support scores from every patch score and map the residual through one global leave-one-out empirical CDF of support residuals, then fuse with MVFA's unchanged rule.

[B1-g1-o4] Matched-support normalisation: normalise each test image against its most similar supports
Instead of per-position statistics (which assume alignment) or a global analytic scale, normalise each test image's branch scores with the leave-one-out scores of the m supports whose global CLIP embedding is closest to it.

[B1-g1-o5] Split-conformal image thresholds from support leave-one-out maxima
Treat the K normal supports as a calibration set: normalise branches by leave-one-out support statistics, compute each support's leave-one-out image score (max of the fused map), and set the operating threshold as a conformal quantile, which bounds the false-positive rate on new normal images by construction.

[B1-g1-o6] Analytic zero-shot scale plus support CDF for the few-shot branch
Normalise MVFA's zero-shot branch without any target data, from the anchor geometry and source-validation statistics, and only the few-shot branch from the K supports via a leave-one-out empirical CDF.

[B1-g2-o1] Alignment-adaptive residual CDF: weighting the positional correction by measured anatomy alignment
Use the residual empirical CDF (positional median subtracted, global CDF of residuals) but weight the positional correction by how much the supports' normal scores actually vary with position, so unaligned modalities fall back to the plain global CDF automatically.

[B1-g2-o2] Feature-registered positional references
Before computing positional statistics, align each support's patch grid to the test image by a small rigid shift found by maximising CLIP patch-feature correlation, so the positional correction of the residual CDF works even where images are only roughly aligned.

[B1-g2-o3] Augmented-support reference sets for inductive normalisation at small K
Enlarge the leave-one-out reference set of every normaliser by scoring label-preserving augmentations of the K normal supports (flips, small shifts and rotations, mild intensity jitter), so the reference distribution reflects normal variability even at K = 2.

[B1-g2-o4] Extreme-value tail extension of the support CDF
Model the upper tail of each branch's leave-one-out support scores with a generalised Pareto distribution, so scores beyond the largest support value are still ordered instead of all mapping to 1, which matters because the image score is the maximum of the fused map.

[B1-g2-o5] Self-referenced residuals: removing each image's own score offset before support-CDF mapping
Subtract from every patch score the median of the same image's own patch scores (a per-image offset reflecting acquisition and intensity) and map the residual through the leave-one-out support CDF of residuals computed the same way, which stays strictly inductive because it uses only the image itself and the supports.

[B1-g2-o6] Similarity-weighted conformal thresholds on residual-CDF scores
Keep residual-CDF scoring but replace the plain split-conformal quantile with a weighted conformal quantile in which supports similar to the test image (CLIP CLS similarity) count more, so the threshold adapts to each image while keeping an approximate false-positive bound under covariate shift.

[B1-g3-o1] Meta-selected normaliser from simulated source episodes
Simulate few-shot episodes on the source modalities, record which inductive normaliser (global CDF, residual CDF, alignment-adaptive residual CDF) works best as a function of support-measurable features (alignment rho, K, score spread), and use this rule to pick the normaliser for the unseen modality from its supports alone.

[B1-g3-o2] Foreground-size-aware Gumbel normalisation of the max-pooled image score
Because the maximum of N normal patch scores grows with N, normalise each image's max fused score by a Gumbel distribution of leave-one-out support maxima whose location is adjusted for the image's number of foreground patches, so large-anatomy images are not systematically scored as more anomalous.

[B1-g3-o3] Optimal-transport correspondence for patch-wise normal references
Instead of grid positions or rigid shifts, match every test patch to support patches by entropic optimal transport over feature and position costs, and normalise its score against the leave-one-out scores of the support patches it is matched to.

[B1-g3-o4] Content-conditioned expected-normal-score regression
Train on the source modalities a small regressor that predicts the expected normal anomaly score of a patch from its frozen CLIP feature, and normalise target scores by the residual from this prediction (re-centred with the supports), removing anatomy-driven offsets without assuming spatial alignment.

[B1-g3-o5] Exact leave-one-out, alignment-adaptive residual CDF
Combine the alignment-adaptive residual CDF (positional correction weighted by measured alignment) with a strictly leave-one-out construction of the support residual references, so the method is safe on unaligned modalities and unbiased at small K.

[B1-g3-o6] Multi-scale positional residuals
Subtract positional medians computed at several grid resolutions (full grid, 2x2-pooled, 4x4-pooled) and map the combined residual through one leave-one-out support CDF, so coarse anatomy offsets and fine structure offsets are removed without estimating each from a few values.
